cur-great-wall-badaling.dateNote: The Badaling section, 70 km north-west of Beijing, guarding the approach to the Juyong Pass, was built in brick and stone in 1505 under the Ming Hongzhi Emperor: about 7.8 m tall, 5.8 m wide on top, with watchtowers along the ridges. Earlier walls held this pass: the Northern Qi built a rammed-earth wall from the Juyong pass in 555, and Xu Da fortified it for the first Ming emperor from 1368. Restored and opened to visitors in 1957. The Great Wall is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987).
